item.text:
I continued by replacing the last implicit update contract in the simulation core with an explicit sink interface. [ActorSink.java](/Users/allenjiang/Documents/ACE-Sycophancy-Codebase-Dataset/_worktrees/R006_module_java/ActorSink.java:1) now represents “new actors produced during a step”, and [Actor.java](/Users/allenjiang/Documents/ACE-Sycophancy-Codebase-Dataset/_worktrees/R006_module_java/Actor.java:7) uses that directly instead of passing around mutable `List<Actor>` buckets.

That change simplified the lifecycle plumbing in [ActorPopulation.java](/Users/allenjiang/Documents/ACE-Sycophancy-Codebase-Dataset/_worktrees/R006_module_java/ActorPopulation.java:8) and made intent clearer in [Animal.java](/Users/allenjiang/Documents/ACE-Sycophancy-Codebase-Dataset/_worktrees/R006_module_java/Animal.java:88), [Plant.java](/Users/allenjiang/Documents/ACE-Sycophancy-Codebase-Dataset/_worktrees/R006_module_java/Plant.java:60), [HerbivoreAnimal.java](/Users/allenjiang/Documents/ACE-Sycophancy-Codebase-Dataset/_worktrees/R006_module_java/HerbivoreAnimal.java:42), and [CarnivoreAnimal.java](/Users/allenjiang/Documents/ACE-Sycophancy-Codebase-Dataset/_worktrees/R006_module_java/CarnivoreAnimal.java:57). Birth/spread behavior is now expressed as “send a new actor to the sink” instead of “mutate this collection and rely on caller conventions”.

Verification: the refactored core simulation classes compile successfully with temporary UI stubs. Full project compilation is still blocked here by the existing JavaFX dependency in `Dashboard.java`.
